detailed_rationale: Waaree Energies is India's largest solar PV module manufacturer (12.6 GW module production in FY26, up from 7.1 GW in FY25) now backward-integrating into cells (2.3 GW produced in FY26 vs 0.1 GW in FY25, targeting ~11.4 GW installed cell capacity by FY27 via G12R lines), plus a 10 GW ingot-wafer facility under construction in Nagpur, and early-stage forays into batteries, inverters and green hydrogen (electrolyzer PLI ~Rs 444cr, hydrogen PLI ~Rs 510cr secured). FY26 revenue mix: Utility/IPP ~34.7%, Overseas ~33%, Retail ~20.8%, EPC ~11.6% -- EPC nearly doubled (Rs 1,559cr to Rs 3,282cr) to become a real second growth leg alongside modules (Rs 12,957cr to Rs 24,133cr, +86.2%). FY26 consolidated: revenue Rs 26,537cr (+84% YoY), EBITDA Rs 5,908cr (+117% YoY, margin 22.3%), PAT Rs 3,884cr (+100% YoY, doubled). Q4FY26 (Mar-2026): PAT Rs 1,126cr (+75% YoY) on total income Rs 8,660cr. Order book stands at ~Rs 53,000cr (~2x FY26 revenue -- healthy book-to-bill), with a >100 GW module-supply pipeline claimed. Management has guided FY27 operating EBITDA of Rs 7,000-7,700cr (+18-30% YoY), a clear deceleration from FY26's 117% EBITDA growth but still a strong absolute number, contingent on the 2H-FY27 cell-capacity ramp landing on schedule -- an execution/timing risk typical of capex-heavy capital-goods names. As of Q1FY27 (Jun-2026), only pre-results analyst estimates are available as of this pass (consolidated PAT ~Rs 950cr est., -10% QoQ, +YoY ~78% on revenue basis per Emkay); the actual print was not located in this research pass and should be confirmed once filed. Two earnings-quality/balance-sheet items stand out. First, a working-capital tell consistent with the execution-ramp pattern this desk watches for: operating cash flow fell from Rs 3,158cr (FY25) to Rs 1,627cr (FY26) even as PAT nearly doubled, driven by inventory surging from Rs 2,692cr to Rs 5,856cr (+117%) -- cash conversion is lagging reported profit growth as the company scales capacity, which is not disqualifying on its own for a fast-growing manufacturer but needs to be watched next 2-3 quarters. Second, Q3FY26 carried a Rs 294.78cr exceptional charge (~5.8% of that quarter's PBT) tied to the ongoing US customs investigation -- a conservative, expense-side one-off (depresses rather than inflates earnings), but it foreshadowed the bigger issue below. The single biggest fresh risk is a US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) final determination (23-Jun-2026) that Waaree evaded AD/CVD orders on solar cells sourced via Vietnam/Malaysia between 2021 and 2026, triggering cash-deposit requirements for anti-dumping duties of up to 271.28% on the flagged shipments; separately, a preliminary US Commerce Department AD determination applies duties up to ~123.04% on India-origin module imports industry-wide. Waaree disputes the CBP finding (says a facility site-visit confirmed no Chinese-origin cells were used) and states US operations continue normally, and is expanding its Texas module facility from 1.6 GW to 3.2 GW regardless -- but this is a live, material, and quantitatively invisible risk sitting inside the ~33% overseas revenue segment and directly under the US capacity-expansion thesis. Valuation: PE ~21.6-21.9x (market cap ~Rs 81,300-85,200cr), down ~27% from the 52-week high (Rs 3,865 -> ~Rs 2,826), broadly matching the quant screen's own pe_for_ranking of 21.93. Quant screen shows top-decile quality (quality_score 81.9, ROE 21.6%, ROCE 25.4%, D/E just 0.22x, interest coverage 21.1x) and top-3% growth scores (growth_3y_score 95.4, growth_1y_score 97.6) alongside a decent value_score of 73.8 -- final_score_3y 75.3 and final_score_1y 63.3, both landing Hold, overall recommendation Hold.
recommendation_rationale: Fundamentals (low leverage, high ROE/ROCE, a ~2x book-to-bill order book, credible FY27 EBITDA guidance) do not support a Sell, and the quant score is already capped at Hold -- under the asymmetric-override rule a Hold cannot be converted to Sell by analyst discretion. I am not rescuing anything (there is nothing to rescue: quant already says Hold) and I am not forcing a Sell despite a real fresh risk (US CBP AD/CVD finding) because the business quality, order book and guidance genuinely justify continued holding pending more clarity on the US exposure -- hence Hold, with an escalation flag so the desk is aware of the tariff development the quant model cannot see.
summary: Waaree Energies delivered another strong year (FY26 revenue +84%, PAT doubled) on the back of rapid capacity scale-up in modules, cells and EPC, and management is guiding a further 18-30% EBITDA increase for FY27 backed by a healthy ~Rs 53,000cr order book. Valuation has cooled to a reasonable ~22x earnings after a roughly 27% pullback from the 52-week high. The main new overhang is a June-2026 US Customs finding that Waaree evaded anti-dumping duties on certain past shipments (potential cash deposits up to ~271% on the flagged volumes), which Waaree disputes; alongside a cash-conversion dip this year (inventory build outpacing profit growth), this is worth watching over the next couple of quarters even though the core business remains high-quality and reasonably valued. Recommendation: Hold.
positive_para: Best-in-class fundamentals for the sector: ROE 21.6%, ROCE 25.4%, D/E only 0.22x, interest coverage 21x -- a rare combination of hyper-growth (FY26 revenue +84%, PAT +100%) with a genuinely under-levered balance sheet. Backward integration into cells (2.3 GW produced in FY26 from near-zero) and a 10 GW ingot-wafer plant reduce import dependence and should support margins as capacity ramps. Order book of ~Rs 53,000cr is roughly 2x FY26 revenue, giving multi-year revenue visibility, and EPC has emerged as a genuine second growth engine (+110% YoY). FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 7,000-7,700cr (+18-30%) is credible given the capacity pipeline, and the stock has already de-rated ~27% from its 52-week high to a PE of ~22x that looks reasonable, not rich, against this growth and quality profile.
negative_para: The US CBP's 23-June-2026 final determination that Waaree evaded AD/CVD orders on certain 2021-2026 shipments (cash deposits up to 271.28% on the flagged volumes) is a genuine, fresh, and material risk sitting directly inside the ~33%-of-revenue overseas segment and the Texas capacity expansion (1.6 GW -> 3.2 GW) that underpins part of the growth story -- Waaree disputes the finding and says US operations are unaffected, but the exposure is real and unresolved. Separately, a broader preliminary US AD determination applies duties up to ~123% on India-origin modules industry-wide, a structural headwind for export ambitions regardless of the CBP-specific dispute. Earnings quality shows an early crack: operating cash flow fell from Rs 3,158cr to Rs 1,627cr in FY26 even as PAT nearly doubled, with inventory up 117% -- a working-capital tell that cash conversion is lagging the P&L as capacity scales, and a pattern this desk watches closely in capex-heavy industrials. FY27 guidance also depends on landing 10 GW of new cell capacity in 2H-FY27 on schedule, an execution-timing risk typical of the sector.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~21.6-21.9x trailing earnings (market cap ~Rs 81,300-85,200cr) for a company that just grew PAT 100% and is guided to grow FY27 EBITDA 18-30%, the multiple is pricing in a meaningful deceleration to something like mid-teens sustained growth over the next several years -- not the hypergrowth pace of FY26. Given the ~2x-revenue order book, ongoing backward integration and a genuine national renewable-capacity tailwind, that implied growth rate looks achievable and the stock reads as fair-to-mildly-cheap post the 27% pullback from its 52-week high, provided the US tariff exposure and cash-conversion dip do not compound. This is not a hypergrowth (>=25%) call, so no dilution/ROE add-on is required.
escalation_reason: The 23-Jun-2026 US CBP final determination (potential AD/CVD cash deposits up to 271.28% on Waaree's 2021-2026 Vietnam/Malaysia-linked shipments, plus a separate ~123% preliminary AD duty on India-origin modules industry-wide) is a live, material, quantitatively-invisible regulatory risk sitting inside the ~33%-of-revenue overseas segment and the Texas capacity-expansion thesis -- the quant score (trailing financials + price/technical factors) has no way to see this. Flagging for the desk/PM to weigh explicitly rather than resolving it myself; fundamentals otherwise support Hold, not Sell.
